raw:
{
  "question_intent": "Inquire about the impact of securitised loans on capital and the effect of hedge allocation on capital efficiency in IB.",
  "main_topics": ["securitised loans", "capital efficiency", "hedge allocation"],
  "answer_completeness": "Complete",
  "response_stance": "Direct",
  "evidence_level": "High",
  "contains_numeric_evidence": true,
  "contains_forward_guidance": false,
  "narrative_alignment": "Aligned",
  "question_quote": "Thank you. First one on USCB, just want to check the offset regarding the securitised loans. Just wondering if we could expect any impact on capital that you are potentially holding on that. The second one would be on the capital efficiency within the IB. Things are important, we noticed also the hedge allocation. So I was just wondering, if the increase in hedge allocation for the IB was actually helping efficiency and to what extent?",
  "answer_quote": "Okay, so let me start with securitised loans. So important to understand that the capital weighting of loans is materially below that of cards. That is true in the UK, it's also true in the US and actually the divergence between UK and US Basel for loans is much less significant than it is in cards. So if you think about why that is, if I lend you money in an unsecured loan, then clearly there is a defined amount of drawdown. With a card, you have a limit and therefore I am required to hold the degree of capital against that limit, irrespective of whether you have drawn on it. So cards are actually a much more significant utiliser of capital. Now, clearly they are much higher margin, but in terms of capital, much more significant. So we would be very, very thoughtful about how we deploy additional capital into this business, but it's not like additional costs, so much, much more efficient. Secondly, in terms of your question on the hedge, on the IB. The hedge allocation on the IB, I think we called it out year on year. So you'll be able to work that out, because you know what the income up lift is from the gross structural hedge income and we've given you the allocation so you'll be able to work out what that number is. It will clearly be a tailwind, but don't think of it as other. It directly relates to the capital that that business is utilising. So it is not a discretionary allocation, it's directly in alignment to those businesses, completely proportional to the RWAs that they are using."
}
